[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Edged is a data center developer and operator, a subsidiary of Endeavour, a holding company building a portfolio of data center operations across Europe and North America. Edged builds and operates what it describes as ultra-efficient, AI-ready facilities for hyperscale cloud companies, technology providers, and large enterprises. Its flagship US facility recorded in this registry, ORD2, sits on a Chicagoland campus in Aurora, Illinois, the first of three planned buildings, which opened February 26, 2025 with a 96 megawatt capacity per the companys own announcement, though third-party directories list an initial 48 megawatt figure, a discrepancy this registry attributes to phased capacity delivery rather than a factual conflict. The facility uses a waterless cooling system the company projects will save nearly 380 million gallons of water annually once the full campus is at capacity, part of a portfolio-wide average power usage effectiveness of 1.15 that Edged markets as a sustainability differentiator against traditional water-cooled data centers. Beyond Chicago, Edged has announced or is developing facilities in Atlanta, Dallas, Kansas City, Columbus, and Phoenix within the United States, along with international sites in Spain and Portugal and planned expansion into France. Edgeds own materials did not publish an exact corporate headquarters city or founding year as of the research date. Its focus on large power-dense AI-ready campuses backed by an institutional holding company parent places it alongside other fast-growing hyperscale-focused developers elsewhere in this registry. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

reading.body:
This facility is Edged's first completed US building on a planned three-building campus in Aurora, Illinois, near Chicago's O'Hare airport. The operator published a 96 megawatt capacity for ORD01 at opening in February 2025, though some third-party sources initially listed 48 megawatts, a gap the operator attributes to phased delivery. At an assumed 40 kilowatts per rack for AI training workloads, 96 megawatts of IT load represents roughly 2,400 racks, a scale typical of purpose-built hyperscale AI facilities rather than traditional colocation campuses.

The facility uses waterless cooling with a reported power usage effectiveness of 1.15, a metric that qualifies it for power-constrained deployments where cooling infrastructure matters as much as electricity supply. The campus location in Illinois places it outside the handful of states where published megawatt figures exist in public operator specs, and ORD01 ranks seventh among only six Illinois facilities with published capacity data, reflecting how little capacity is formally declared in the state despite 44 mapped data center sites.

Edged announced three buildings planned for this Aurora campus, but only ORD01's opening is published. The second and third phases remain unannounced in the operator's public materials, meaning total eventual campus size cannot be determined from the facts available. The facility matters to AI scaling primarily as a proof point that new hyperscale-focused developers are delivering power-dense buildings where the grid can supply them, rather than as a standalone constraint on national AI capacity.
